mainTopic: Who owns a stray dove chick found near a dovecote, and how the גמרא weighs רוב (the majority) against קרוב (closeness) when deciding an unclear case.
overview: The משנה rules that a young dove found within fifty אמות of a שובך belongs to the owner of that שובך, and one found farther away belongs to the finder. If it is found between two dovecotes, it goes to the closer one, and if it is exactly in the middle, the owners split it. רבי חנינא then teaches that when רוב and קרוב point different ways, we follow רוב, even though both are דאורייתא. רבי זירא challenges this from עגלה ערופה, where the Torah picks the closest city. The גמרא answers that there is no bigger city, and the city sits alone between mountains. Next the גמרא challenges רבי חנינא from our משנה. It answers that the first case has only one dovecote, and a hopping chick cannot go past fifty אמות. רבי ירמיה asks about a chick with one leg on each side of the line, and he is sent out of the בית מדרש. Finally the case of two dovecotes is explained as two equal dovecotes. The גמרא asks why we do not follow the majority of the world, and its answer begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Who owns a stray dove chick found near a dovecote
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a chick found within fifty אמות of a שובך belongs to the owner of the שובך. Beyond that, it belongs to the finder. Between two dovecotes, it goes to the closer one, and if it is equally distant, the owners split it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A chick found within fifty אמות of a dovecote belongs to the dovecote's owner. One found beyond fifty אמות belongs to the person who finds it. If it was found between two dovecotes: if it is closer to this one, it belongs to this one's owner; if it is closer to that one, it belongs to that one's owner. If it is exactly halfway, the two owners divide it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the rules for who owns a young dove found on the ground near a dovecote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses distance to decide ownership. Close by (within fifty אמות), we assume the chick hopped out of the nearby שובך. Farther away, we can no longer tie it to that שובך, so the finder keeps it. With two dovecotes, the closer one wins, and if neither is closer, they split it.

keyTerms.meaning: A young dove chick that cannot yet fly well and hops along the ground
A dovecote, the structure where doves live
A cubit, a measure of length (roughly half a meter)

steps.whatToRemember: Within fifty אמות the chick goes to the owner of the שובך. Beyond fifty it goes to the finder. Between two dovecotes it goes to the closer one, and if it is equally far from both, the owners split it.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A dove chick that was found within fifty cubits of a dovecote,
it belongs to the owner of the dovecote.
If it was found beyond fifty cubits,
it belongs to the one who finds it.
If it was found between two dovecotes:
if it is close to this one, it belongs to this one's owner.
If it is close to that one, it belongs to that one's owner.
If it is half and half, the two of them divide it.
phrases.notes: Half and half means it is the same distance from both dovecotes.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נִיפּוּל הַנִּמְצָא בְּתוֹךְ חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A chick within fifty אמות belongs to the owner of the שובך, beyond that it belongs to the finder, and between two dovecotes it goes to the closer one (or is split if equidistant).

steps.title: When majority and closeness conflict, follow the majority
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא rules that when רוב (majority) and קרוב (closeness) point in different directions, we follow רוב. This holds even though both principles come from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי חנינא says: When there is a conflict between majority and closeness, we follow the majority. And even though majority is from the Torah and closeness is from the Torah, even so, majority is stronger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a general rule from רבי חנינא about which principle wins when רוב and קרוב disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes we must decide where an unclear item came from. One way is to look at where most such items come from (רוב). Another way is to look at what it is closest to (קרוב). רבי חנינא says that when the two clash, רוב wins, even though both are equally דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Majority, meaning we follow what is true of most cases
Closeness, meaning we assume the item belongs to whatever is nearest
From the Torah itself (not a rabbinic rule)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think closeness is weaker because it is only rabbinic. רבי חנינא says clearly that both are דאורייתא, and still רוב wins.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule becomes the measuring stick for the rest of the סוגיא. Every source the גמרא brings next is checked against it.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Ḥanina says:
Majority and proximity,
phrases.notes: He means a case where these two point to different answers.

phrases.english: we follow the majority.
And even though majority is a Torah principle
and proximity is a Torah principle,
even so, majority is preferable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא רוֹב וְקָרוֹב הוֹלְכִין אַחַר הָרוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a general principle about רוב versus קרוב, which relates to the משנה's use of closeness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When רוב and קרוב conflict, follow רוב, even though both are דאורייתא.

steps.title: Challenge from the closest city in עגלה ערופה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges רבי חנינא from the Torah's law of עגלה ערופה. There the Torah tells us to go by the city closest to the dead body, even if another city is bigger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא raised an objection: 'And it shall be, the city that is nearest to the slain man' — and this is so even though there may be another city that is bigger than it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks רבי חנינא's rule using a פסוק that seems to follow closeness instead of majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a murdered body is found and the killer is unknown, the Torah makes the nearest city bring the עגלה ערופה. If רוב were stronger, we should blame the bigger city, since most people (and so most likely the killer) come from there. The פסוק follows closeness, which seems to contradict רבי חנינא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira raises an objection:
"And it shall be, the city that is nearest to the slain man"
and this is so even though there is another city
that is larger than it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי חנינא's rule from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's rule that רוב beats קרוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah follows the closest city for עגלה ערופה even when a bigger city exists, so closeness seems to beat majority.

steps.title: The case is where no bigger city exists
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is talking about a case where no other city is bigger than the closest one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about where there is no bigger city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי חנינא by narrowing the case of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the closest city is also the biggest, רוב and קרוב point to the same city. Then there is no conflict, and the פסוק does not prove that closeness beats majority.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where there is not (any bigger city)

phrases.english: It is referring to where there is no such larger city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case so there is no conflict between רוב and קרוב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to choose the closest city even over a bigger one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק speaks where the closest city is also the biggest, so it says nothing against רבי חנינא.

steps.title: Why not follow the majority of the whole world
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: even if no single city is bigger, most people in the world live elsewhere, so we should follow that majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us follow the majority of the world!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the closest city is the biggest single city, all the other people in the world together are more than that city. By רבי חנינא's rule, that world majority should beat closeness, so the problem comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: The majority of the world (most people everywhere)

phrases.english: But let us follow the majority of the world!
phrases.notes: Meaning: most people live outside this city, so the killer probably came from somewhere else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that no bigger city exists.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rest of the world together is still a majority, so by רבי חנינא's rule we should follow it rather than the closest city.

steps.title: The city sits alone between mountains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is a city cut off between mountains, so no outside majority is realistically involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a city that sits between the mountains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the case even further to save רבי חנינא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A city hidden between mountains is cut off from the rest of the world. People from elsewhere are unlikely to reach it, so the world majority does not count. Closeness is the only factor left, and this does not contradict the rule that רוב beats קרוב.
steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק of עגלה ערופה follows the closest city only where there is no competing majority: no bigger city, and the city is isolated between mountains. So רבי חנינא's rule that רוב beats קרוב still stands.

phrases.english: It is referring to a city that sits between the mountains.
phrases.notes: Mountains cut the city off, so outsiders rarely get there.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Further limiting the case so that no majority competes with closeness.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The majority of the world should outweigh the closest city.
steps.terutzMaskana: The city is isolated between mountains, so the world majority is not relevant and רבי חנינא's rule stands.

steps.title: A challenge from the baby dove found near a dovecote
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה that gives a chick found within fifty אמות to the owner of the nearby שובך, even if another dovecote is bigger. That looks like following קרוב over רוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: a baby dove found within fifty אמות belongs to the owner of the dovecote. But maybe there is another dovecote that is bigger than this one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to רבי חנינא, this time from a משנה about a stray baby dove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the chick to the nearest dovecote and makes no exception. That suggests we follow closeness even when a bigger dovecote nearby has more birds. This goes against רבי חנינא, who says רוב wins.

keyTerms.meaning: A young dove that cannot yet fly properly
Dovecote, a structure where doves live

phrases.english: We learned: a baby dove that is found
within fifty cubits
belongs to the owner of the dovecote;
and that is so even though there is
another dovecote that is bigger than it!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: נִיפּוּל הַנִּמְצָא בְּתוֹךְ חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the עגלה ערופה challenge was resolved, a new source is brought against רבי חנינא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's rule that רוב beats קרוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה follows the nearest dovecote without exception, even when another dovecote is bigger, so closeness seems to win.

steps.title: No other dovecote is around
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a case where there is no other dovecote nearby.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where there isn't another one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה only speaks about a place with no other dovecote, so there is no majority to compete with closeness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is only one dovecote, closeness and majority point the same way. So the משנה does not prove that closeness beats majority.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where there isn't (another one)

phrases.english: It is where there isn't one.
phrases.notes: He means there isn't any other dovecote around at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה applies even when a bigger dovecote is nearby.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is only about a place with one dovecote, so no majority is in play.

steps.title: Then why does the finder keep it beyond fifty?
steps.stepSummary: If there is only one dovecote, a chick found beyond fifty אמות must also have come from it. So why does the משנה give it to the finder?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end of the משנה: beyond fifty אמות, it belongs to the finder. But if there is no other dovecote, it surely fell from that one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 8 by using the second half of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is only one dovecote in the area, any stray chick should belong to it, however far away it is found. Yet the משנה says the finder keeps it beyond fifty אמות. So the 'only one dovecote' answer seems not to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (look at) the end of the משנה

phrases.english: If so, say the end part:
beyond fifty cubits
it belongs to its finder.
But if there isn't another dovecote,
it surely fell from that one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה speaks of a case with no other dovecote
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With only one dovecote, even a chick found far away must belong to its owner, yet the משנה gives it to the finder.

steps.title: A hopping chick can't hop beyond fifty
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is about a chick that only hops. Such a chick cannot get farther than fifty אמות, so one found farther away did not come from this dovecote on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? A chick that hops. As רב עוקבא בר חמא said: anything that hops does not hop more than fifty אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its answer by explaining the case: the chick hops and cannot fly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hopping chick physically cannot hop past fifty אמות. So a chick found farther away did not hop there from this dovecote; someone else must have brought it. That is why the finder keeps it, even though there is only one dovecote.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
Hops or walks step by step (cannot fly yet)

steps.whatToRemember: Within fifty אמות the chick goes to the dovecote owner because there is no other dovecote and a hopping chick can reach that far. Beyond fifty, it could not have hopped there, so the finder keeps it.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
With a chick that hops,
as רב עוקבא בר חמא said:
any creature that hops
does not hop more than fifty cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 and keeps the answer of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case further, with a supporting statement of an אמורא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With one dovecote, any chick found anywhere must have come from it.
steps.terutzMaskana: A hopping chick cannot pass fifty אמות, so a chick found farther away came some other way and the finder keeps it.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה's question about one leg on each side
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks what the law is if the chick has one leg inside the fifty אמות and one leg outside. The גמרא reports that for this question he was put out of the בית מדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: if one of its legs is within fifty אמות and one leg is beyond fifty אמות, what is the law? And because of this they removed רבי ירמיה from the בית מדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks a question about the fifty-אמה line, and then the גמרא tells us he was sent out of the בית מדרש because of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question tests whether the fifty-אמה line is an exact cut-off. The other חכמים reacted by removing him, and the גמרא leaves the question without an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked, raised a question to be resolved

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not answered here, and it is not part of the back-and-forth about רוב and קרוב. It is a side question about the fifty-אמה line.

phrases.english: רבי ירמיה asked:
if one of its legs is within fifty cubits,
and one of its legs is beyond fifty cubits,
what is the law?
And for this they took him out:
רבי ירמיה, from the study hall.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: מסקנא (the closing comment about his removal)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question about the fifty-אמה boundary from step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which side of the line counts when the chick stands across the fifty-אמה boundary.

steps.title: A challenge from a chick found between two dovecotes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a chick found between two dovecotes goes to whichever one is closer, even if the other dovecote is bigger. That again looks like closeness beating majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if it was found between two dovecotes, if it is closer to this one it is his, and if closer to that one it is his. And that is so even though one of them is bigger than the other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main question and brings another part of the משנה as a challenge to רבי חנינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time there really are two dovecotes, so the answer 'there is no other one' cannot work. The משנה follows the closer dovecote and makes no exception for a bigger one. That seems to show קרוב beats רוב.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
if it was found between two dovecotes,
if close to this one, it is his,
and if close to that one, it is his;
and that is so even though one of them
is bigger than the other!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: נִמְצָא בֵּין שְׁנֵי שׁוֹבָכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from רבי ירמיה's side question to challenging רבי חנינא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's rule that רוב beats קרוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With two dovecotes, the משנה follows the closer one with no exception, even if the other has more birds.

steps.title: The two dovecotes are the same size
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about two dovecotes that are equal in size.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where the two dovecotes are equal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about two dovecotes of equal size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both dovecotes have the same number of birds, there is no majority between them. So closeness decides, and רבי חנינא's rule is not contradicted.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where the two of them are equal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה follows the closer dovecote even when the other is bigger.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dovecotes are equal, so there is no majority between them and closeness decides.

steps.title: What about the majority of the world?
steps.stepSummary: Even if the two dovecotes are equal, all the other dovecotes in the world together are a majority. So why not follow them?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us follow the majority of the world!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of step 13, just like it did with עגלה ערופה in step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Equal size only removes a majority between these two dovecotes. Most of the doves in the world live in other dovecotes, so following רוב should take the chick away from both owners.

phrases.english: But let us go after the majority of the world!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 13, using the same reasoning as step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the two dovecotes are equal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rest of the world's dovecotes together are a majority, so following רוב should beat closeness.

steps.title: The answer begins: what case is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens its answer by asking what case the משנה is about. The rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its answer to the 'majority of the world' challenge. It is about to describe the exact case, and that description comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'הכא במאי עסקינן' tells us an answer is coming that will narrow the case. We expect it to explain why the world's majority is not a real factor here, like the mountain answer in step 6.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, where the גמרא describes the case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא), the answer continues in the next section
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The world's majority should decide where the chick came from.
steps.terutzMaskana: Stated on the next amud, where the case is defined.
